mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 60-day forward returns in downturn periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or 60-day forward returns in GDP decline periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 5-day forward returns in recovery periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer and construction activity boost economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods with increased housing starts and consumption, or 20-day forward returns in these periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 60-day forward returns in these periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over two consecutive months signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased employment supports consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
